messages:
maria: FYI, ACME reported that after the nightly SCIM sync ~2k users were present but only ~300 got roles assigned. They say group->role mapping used to work.

jenny: do we have the SCIM logs? error snippets?

maria: pasted the relevant snippet from our logs (sanitized):
```
2026-03-12T03:12:05Z WARN scim-provisioner request_id=req_9f2e
PATCH /scim/v2/Groups/00a1-members
401/403 response: 403 {"detail":"insufficient_scope","schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:error:2.0:Error"]}
payload: {"Operations":[{"op":"add","path":"members","value":[{"value":"8af3c2d","display":"jdoe@example.com","$ref":"/Users/8af3c2d"}]}]}
```

maria: customer says they recently rotated their Okta provisioning token; they mentioned it was an OAuth client token, not an API key.

ben: 403 + "insufficient_scope" during PATCH strongly smells like the token used for SCIM doesn't have write/group scopes. Okta often gives distinct scopes for `scim.read` vs `scim.write` or the app-level provisioning scope is disabled.

sam: also worth checking externalId/member id mismatch. If group members reference users by an opaque member id that changed during their user merge/duplicate resolution, our group patch might reference non-existing user IDs and we could drop the mapping silently. Do we see any 404 user not found earlier?

maria: no 404s in the logs, just 403s for group member PATCH. But customer also said they merged two Okta profiles last week which changed their internal member ids. Could be related.

jenny: action items: 1) get the exact token string (or token id) used by ACME for provisioning 2) check the OAuth client scope set in Okta 3) request a full provisioning audit export from their Okta side (member ids before/after merge) 4) replicate with a scoped token in our test tenant.

maria: I asked ACME to paste the token ID and screenshot of the app assignment scopes. They sent a redacted screenshot showing only scope names: `scim.read`, `user.read`, `group.read` — notably missing `scim.write` / `group.write`.

ben: that would explain it. If PATCH calls are authenticated by a token lacking write scope Okta will respond 403. For now they attempted automatic rollback which left groups in a half-applied state.

sam: recommended quick mitigation to ACME: create a new OAuth token/client with provisioning enabled for `scim.write` and `group.write`, then rotate the credential in our console and trigger a manual full sync from our side. Steps I sent them: 
```
1) In Okta admin > Applications > {Redwood SCIM app} > Assign > Create Token (ensure Provisioning: Push groups and Push users enabled)
2) In Redwood Console > Customer > Integrations > SCIM > Edit > Paste token > Save
3) In Console > SCIM > Actions > Trigger full resync (this will re-apply group->role mapping)
```

maria: ACME followed the steps. They created a new token, updated ours, and we retried the full sync. During retry we saw the scim-provisioner job post a background task. scim-bot posted: 
```
scim-bot: job started job_id=job_34a2 full_sync user_count=2314
```

jenny: good. Any errors during retry?

maria: initial passes showed success on PATCH after token update. Sample successful PATCH log: 
```
2026-03-12T03:41:10Z INFO scim-provisioner request_id=req_9f2e
PATCH /scim/v2/Groups/00a1-members 200
applied members: ["8af3c2d","bb12ff4","c3e9a00"]
```

ben: follow-up: the root cause ended up being twofold: 1) token scope was insufficient (missing write scope) 2) the Okta profile merge produced a new opaque member id for ~120 users; our provisioning path uses the `value` field (Okta user id) when reconciling group memberships. If the patch references the old id and the provider refuses to translate/reconcile, group finish may be partial.

sam: we should add defensive logic: when a group PATCH fails due to 403/insufficient_scope, surface a clear actionable error in the Console UI telling customers to check provisioning token scopes (link to docs), and when we detect member ids not found during full sync attempt a fallback flow: try matching by email and queue up a member-rewrite so the group patch uses current user ids.

jenny: agreed. I'll file a short ticket and add two items: 
- UX message + docs link about token scopes (owner: jenny)
- Sync fallback prototype that does email-to-user-id lookup and retries group application (owner: ben)

maria: ACME confirmed after the full sync all missing roles are assigned. They also asked if future Okta merges will re-break mapping — we told them new merges that change Okta user id will require either us to reconcile by email or for them to run a full sync after the merge.

ben: for immediate reliability, we should run the fallback prototype as a non-default flag on next full sync and monitor for false positives (email collisions).

maria: closing the customer ticket once we have the docs link. ACME is happy. I'll follow up with the customer success write-up and add notes to the account: "rotated provisioning token lacked write scope; merged user ids caused partial mapping; full sync with new token fixed it."

scim-bot: job completed job_id=job_34a2 status=success elapsed=00:03:12

maria: thanks everyone.

sam: filing an incident-proofing task for the fallback logic and a small Console UX change.

jenny: adding docs entry: https://docs.redwood.ai/scim#token-scopes (draft)

maria: marking resolved for customer; will post the account notes in zendesk.
